In [[algebraic topology]], the '''Hopf construction''' constructs a map from the [[join (topology)|join]] <math>X*Y</math> of two spaces ''<math>X</math>'' and ''<math>Y</math>'' to the [[suspension (topology)|suspension]] ''<math>SZ</math>'' of a space <math>Z</math> out of a map from <math>X\times Y</math> to ''<math>Z</math>''. It was introduced by {{harvs|txt|last=Hopf|authorlink=Heinz Hopf|year=1935}} in the case when ''<math>X</math>'' and ''<math>Y</math>'' are spheres. {{harvtxt|Whitehead|1942}} used it to define the [[J-homomorphism]].

==Construction==

The Hopf construction can be obtained as the composition of a map
:''<math>X*Y\rightarrow S(X\times Y)</math>''
and the suspension
:''<math>S(X\times Y)\rightarrow SZ</math>''
of the map from <math>X\times Y</math> to ''<math>Z</math>''.

The map from <math>X*Y</math> to ''<math>S(X\times Y)</math>'' can be obtained by regarding both sides as a quotient of <math>X\times Y\times I</math> where ''<math>I</math>'' is the unit interval. For <math>X*Y</math> one identifies <math>(x,y,0)</math> with <math>(z,y,0)</math> and <math>(x,y,1)</math> with <math>(x,z,1)</math>, while for ''<math>S(X\times Y)</math>'' one contracts all points of the form <math>(x,y,0)</math> to a point and also contracts all points of the form <math>(x,y,1)</math> to a point. So the map from <math>X\times Y\times I</math> to ''<math>S(X\times Y)</math>'' factors through <math>X*Y</math>.
